abstracts.value: The incorporation of Wilson lines leads to an extension of the modular symmetries of string compactification beyond <math altimg="si2.svg"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">SL</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>. In the simplest case with one Wilson line Z, Kähler modulus T and complex structure modulus U, we are led to the Siegel modular group <math altimg="si3.svg"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Sp</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>. It includes <math altimg="si4.svg"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">SL</mi></mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo>×</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">SL</mi></mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>U</mi></mrow></msub></math> as well as <math altimg="si122.svg"><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="double-struck">Z</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> mirror symmetry, which interchanges T and U. Possible applications to flavor physics of the Standard Model require the study of orbifolds of <math altimg="si3.svg"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Sp</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> to obtain chiral fermions. We identify the 13 possible orbifolds and determine their modular flavor symmetries as subgroups of <math altimg="si3.svg"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Sp</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>. Some cases correspond to symmetric orbifolds that extend previously discussed cases of <math altimg="si2.svg"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">SL</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math>. Others are based on asymmetric orbifold twists (including mirror symmetry) that do no longer allow for a simple intuitive geometrical interpretation and require further study. Sometimes they can be mapped back to symmetric orbifolds with quantized Wilson lines. The symmetries of <math altimg="si3.svg"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Sp</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></math> reveal exciting new aspects of modular symmetries with promising applications to flavor model building.

The incorporation of Wilson lines leads to an extension of the modular symmetries of string compactification beyond $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb Z)$. In the simplest case with one Wilson line $Z$, Kähler modulus $T$ and complex structure modulus $U$, we are led to the Siegel modular group $\mathrm{Sp}(4,\mathbb Z)$. It includes $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb Z)_T\times\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb Z)_U$ as well as $\mathbb Z_2$ mirror symmetry, which interchanges $T$ and $U$. Possible applications to flavor physics of the Standard Model require the study of orbifolds of $\mathrm{Sp}(4,\mathbb Z)$ to obtain chiral fermions. We identify the 13 possible orbifolds and determine their modular flavor symmetries as subgroups of $\mathrm{Sp}(4,\mathbb Z)$. Some cases correspond to symmetric orbifolds that extend previously discussed cases of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb Z)$. Others are based on asymmetric orbifold twists (including mirror symmetry) that do no longer allow for a simple intuitive geometrical interpretation and require further study. Sometimes they can be mapped back to symmetric orbifolds with quantized Wilson lines. The symmetries of $\mathrm{Sp}(4,\mathbb Z)$ reveal exciting new aspects of modular symmetries with promising applications to flavor model building.
